title: Platform crop-relative water demand vs measured greenhouse lettuce evapotranspiration

excluded.flagAboveIrrigationCeiling: 6 pot-days above the study's 350 mL/pot/day ceiling
excluded.outOfPublication: 4 autoclaved treatments marked unused by the publication

scalePerPot.interpretation: On the pot-surface denominator the platform's crop-relative demand is about a seventh of the measured pot water use, and the fitted scale is consistent across treatments (a 0.73 spread over a 6.34 level), so it is not a per-treatment artefact - but see denominatorSensitivity, where the same data on a canopy-area denominator reverses the sign of the discrepancy. Note what the scaled fit cannot be read as: a fitted scale of N is not evidence that peak water use is N times the profile value, because the same constant also absorbs the pot-area assumption, the untranspiring substrate surface, and the fact that evapotranspiration includes evaporation.

shape.note: A high rank correlation with a large level error means the growth curve has the right season but the wrong magnitude; the two findings must be read together.

perGramFreshMass.interpretation: Fresh mass is the denominator the dataset actually supports: it is measured per plant, it is what the platform's growth model predicts, and it does not depend on the unpublished pot diameter. It does not remove the evaporation component.

leafArea.source: data/processed/phase26/greenlight2024_lettuce_harvest.csv (different experiment, different cultivar, so a cross-experiment order-of-magnitude check only)
leafArea.suspectedUnitError: the sheet's 'leafAreaMm2' mean is 1298, which read literally is 0.0013 m2 for a 48 g lettuce with 20 leaves of 158 x 123 mm. Reconstructing 20 leaves of the simultaneously reported dimensions gives ~1350 cm2, so the column is numerically consistent with cm2 and off by 100x against its own unit label. Treated here as cm2 and labelled as an inference, not as a correction of the publisher's file.

freshMass.unit: mL per g fresh mass per day
freshMass.basis: fresh mass at harvest, no area needed

denominatorSensitivity.conclusion: Against the platform's own 2.5 L/m2/day lettuce flux: on the pot-surface assumption measured water use is 4x the profile, and on a canopy-area assumption it is 0.37x the profile - the sign of the finding reverses with the denominator the study does not publish. The spread between those two readings is larger than either discrepancy. This dataset therefore cannot identify a level correction, and no constant may be changed on the strength of it. What does survive is the shape, which is denominator-free.
consequenceForThePlatform: the demand path is documented as unvalidated in level and partially supported in shape

why: evapotranspiration is measured; transpiration is not separated from substrate evaporation
no per-day weather is published for the trial, so no reference ET0 and no crop coefficient can be derived
one cultivar, one greenhouse, four weeks, pot culture: this is a benchmark, not an operating-condition dataset
the trial ran on Earth; nothing here is a reduced-gravity observation
canItCloseTheGap.blockedBy: an unpublished geometric quantity (pot spacing / canopy area) that no downstream analysis can recover from this file
canItCloseTheGap.whatItDoesClose: the 'no measured crop water use exists anywhere in the repository' half of the gap. A per-plant, per-day, replicated measurement now exists in-repo with its licence and hash, and the platform's water demand is compared against it in a committed, reproducible artefact. The gap's remaining blockers are the ones listed above, and they are not addressable from this dataset.

notClaimed: no crop coefficient is published or implied
no validation accuracy: this is an out-of-sample comparison against a third-party measurement, not a model score
no claim that the simulator was corrected: the profile constants are untouched
